VAT-001.q: Under the 2024 VAT Law, objects subject to VAT are:
o: Goods and services used for production, business and consumption in Vietnam, except those not subject to VAT
VAT-001.e: Article 3 of the VAT Law: taxable objects are goods and services used for production, business and consumption in Vietnam (including those bought from foreign organisations/individuals), except the non-taxable objects in Article 5.
VAT-001.x:
Basis: Article 3 of VAT Law 48/2024/QH15 – taxable objects are goods and services used for production, business and consumption in Vietnam, including those bought from foreign organisations and individuals, except the non-taxable items listed in Article 5.
Distractors: B and C narrow the scope (VAT covers both imports and domestic output); D is wrong because many receipts that are not sale prices of goods or services (e.g., compensation, dividends) are not declared for VAT.
Note: Analyse any transaction in order: is it a taxable supply → is it non-taxable under Article 5 → which rate under Article 9.

VAT-002.q: Unprocessed livestock products sold by the organisation or individual who raised them fall under which treatment?
VAT-002.e: Unprocessed or only ordinarily pre-processed crop, planted-forest, livestock and aquatic products sold by their producer, and at the import stage, are not subject to VAT.
VAT-002.x:
Basis: Article 5(1) of Law 48/2024/QH15 (amended by Law 149/2025/QH15) – crop, livestock and aquatic products not processed into other products or only ordinarily pre-processed, sold by those who produce them and at the import stage, are not subject to VAT.
Analysis: The two decisive conditions are (1) unprocessed or ordinarily pre-processed and (2) sold by the producer. If either fails, consider the 5% rate or the 'no need to declare and pay' mechanism.
Distractors: 5%, 10% and 0% apply only to taxable goods; 0% is for exports.

VAT-003.q: From 01/01/2026 a trading company buys green coffee beans (only dried and hulled) from farmers and sells them to a processing company. How is this sale treated?
o: No VAT is declared or paid on the sale, but input VAT is deductible
Not subject to VAT and no input VAT deduction
VAT-003.e: Law 149/2025/QH15: when an enterprise or cooperative buys unprocessed (or ordinarily pre-processed) agricultural products and sells them to another enterprise or cooperative, it does not declare or pay VAT on that sale but may deduct input VAT.
VAT-003.x:
Basis: Law 149/2025/QH15 amending the VAT Law, effective 01/01/2026 – enterprises and cooperatives buying unprocessed or ordinarily pre-processed crop, livestock and aquatic products to sell to other enterprises or cooperatives need not declare and pay output VAT but may credit input VAT.
Analysis: Green coffee only dried and hulled is ordinary pre-processing; the buyer is a processing enterprise → the 'no need to declare and pay' mechanism applies. Unlike 'non-taxable', input VAT remains creditable.
Distractors: A and D apply when selling to households/consumers (5%) or for processed goods (10%); C confuses it with non-taxable status, losing the input credit.

VAT-004.q: Unprocessed agricultural products at the commercial stage sold to a household business or a consumer are taxed at:
VAT-004.e: At the commercial stage, raw agricultural products sold to household/individual businesses and consumers remain at 5%; only sales between enterprises/cooperatives are exempt from declaring and paying.
VAT-004.x:
Basis: Law 48/2024/QH15 as amended by Law 149/2025/QH15; Decree 181/2025/ND-CP (amended by Decree 359/2025/ND-CP).
Analysis: The 'no need to declare and pay' mechanism applies only between enterprises and cooperatives. When a trader sells raw farm produce to household businesses, individuals or consumers, the goods remain taxable at the 5% rate for unprocessed agricultural products at the trading stage.
Distractors: 0% is only for exports; 8% is the reduced rate for the 10% group, not the 5% group; 10% is the standard rate, not the rate for raw produce.

VAT-005.q: From 01/7/2025 to 31/12/2025, a trading company selling unprocessed agricultural products to another enterprise had to charge 5% VAT.
VAT-005.e: True. Law 48/2024/QH15 applied 5% at the commercial stage in that period; from 01/01/2026 Law 149/2025/QH15 restored the 'no declaration, but input VAT deductible' mechanism.
VAT-005.x:
Basis: Law 48/2024/QH15 (effective 01/07/2025) and Law 149/2025/QH15 (applicable from 01/01/2026).
Analysis: In the second half of 2025, Law 48/2024 removed the 'no need to declare and pay' mechanism at the trading stage, so traders selling raw produce to other enterprises charged 5%. From 01/01/2026, Law 149/2025 restored the old mechanism.
Note: Such questions test effective dates – always identify the transaction date before choosing the applicable text.

VAT-006.q: Breeding cattle and breeding calves sold by an enterprise fall under which VAT treatment?
VAT-006.e: Livestock breeds and plant varieties (breeding animals, breeding eggs, seedlings, seeds…) are not subject to VAT.
VAT-006.x:
Basis: Article 5 of Law 48/2024/QH15 – livestock breeds and plant varieties (breeding animals, eggs, seedlings, seeds, genetic material…) are not subject to VAT.
Analysis: Breeding cattle and calves are livestock breeds and are non-taxable at every stage (production, trading, import), unlike commercial livestock products at the trading stage.
Distractors: 5% applies to animal feed; 10% is the standard rate; 0% is the export rate.

VAT-007.q: From 01/7/2025, animal feed moved from 'not subject to VAT' to:
VAT-007.e: Law 48/2024/QH15 moved animal feed, fertiliser, specialised agricultural machinery and offshore fishing vessels to the 5% rate, so their input VAT becomes deductible.
VAT-007.x:
Basis: Article 9 of Law 48/2024/QH15 – from 01/07/2025 animal feed, fertiliser, specialised agricultural machinery and offshore fishing vessels move to the 5% rate.
Analysis: The policy aim is to let producers credit and reclaim input VAT (when non-taxable, input VAT had to be expensed, raising costs).
Distractors: 0% is for exports only; 8% is a temporary reduction for the 10% group; 10% is not the statutory rate for these goods.

VAT-008.q: Select ALL items that moved from 'not subject to VAT' to the 5% rate under the 2024 VAT Law:
o: Machinery and equipment specialised for agricultural production
VAT-008.e: Fertiliser, animal feed and specialised agricultural machinery (and offshore fishing vessels) are taxed at 5%; livestock breeds and credit services remain non-taxable.
VAT-008.x:
Basis: Articles 5 and 9 of Law 48/2024/QH15.
Analysis: Three groups moved from 'non-taxable' to 5%: fertiliser; animal feed; specialised agricultural machinery and equipment (plus offshore fishing vessels).
Distractors: Livestock breeds remain non-taxable (Article 5); credit services remain non-taxable as financial services under Article 5.

VAT-009.q: From the 2026 tax period, goods and services of household/individual businesses are not subject to VAT if annual revenue does not exceed:
VAT-009.e: Law 09/2026/QH16 lets the Government set the threshold; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP raised it to VND 1 billion/year (Law 149/2025 had set 500 million, Law 48/2024 200 million).
VAT-009.x:
Basis: Law 09/2026/QH16 amended Article 5(25) of the VAT Law, delegating the threshold to the Government; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP sets VND 1 billion/year from the 2026 tax period.
Analysis: Household and individual businesses with annual revenue of VND 1 billion or less are not subject to VAT.
Distractors: 200 million was the Law 48/2024 threshold; 500 million was Law 149/2025's; 3 billion is a PIT grouping threshold for household businesses, not the VAT exemption threshold.

VAT-010.q: Arrange chronologically the annual revenue thresholds below which household/individual businesses are not subject to VAT:
o: VND 100 million (2008 VAT Law and amendments)
VAT-010.e: The threshold rose with each amendment; from the 2026 tax period it is VND 1 billion/year.
VAT-010.x:
Basis: The 2008 VAT Law and amendments; Law 48/2024/QH15; Law 149/2025/QH15; Law 09/2026/QH16 and Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: The threshold rose 100 million → 200 million → 500 million → 1 billion VND, reflecting the policy of reducing compliance burdens on small household businesses as they move to self-declaration and e-invoices.
Note: For earlier years, use the threshold in force for that tax period.

VAT-011.q: Lending (credit) services of credit institutions are:
VAT-011.e: Credit services are not subject to VAT.
VAT-011.x:
Basis: Article 5 of Law 48/2024/QH15 – credit services are financial and banking services not subject to VAT.
Analysis: Loan interest isn't VAT-taxable revenue, so credit institutions can't credit related input VAT (shared inputs must be apportioned).
Distractors: 10%, 5% and 0% all assume a taxable service.

VAT-012.q: Transfer of land use rights is:
o: Taxed at 10% on the full transfer price
VAT-012.e: Transfer of land use rights is not subject to VAT; in real-estate business the land price is deducted from the VAT base.
VAT-012.x:
Basis: Articles 5 and 7 of Law 48/2024/QH15 – transfers of land use rights are not subject to VAT; in property business, the land price is deducted from the VAT base.
Analysis: When selling a house with land, the building and infrastructure are taxable while the deductible land value is excluded (see VAT-056).
Distractors: A taxes the land value, which is wrong; 5% and 0% are not rules for land use rights.

VAT-013.q: Medical examination, treatment and disease-prevention services for humans are not subject to VAT.
VAT-013.e: True. Medical services are non-taxable under Article 5 of the VAT Law.
VAT-013.x:
Basis: Article 5 of Law 48/2024/QH15 – medical services (examination, treatment and prevention for humans), elderly and disability care services, etc., are not subject to VAT.
Analysis: True. Distinguish from medicines and medical equipment, which are goods taxed at 5% (VAT-040).

VAT-014.q: Teaching and vocational training provided in accordance with the law are taxed at 5% VAT.
VAT-014.e: False. Teaching and vocational training under the law are not subject to VAT.
VAT-014.x:
Basis: Article 5 of Law 48/2024/QH15 – teaching and vocational training under the law are not subject to VAT.
Analysis: False – they are non-taxable, not 5%. Ancillary school supplies (e.g., uniforms, space rental) may be taxable on their own nature.

o: Taxed at 0% even when consumed domestically
VAT-015.e: Technology transfer, transfer of intellectual property rights and computer software are not subject to VAT.
VAT-015.x:
Basis: Article 5 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Decree 181/2025/ND-CP – technology transfer, IP transfers and computer software are not subject to VAT.
Analysis: Software products (and software services as defined) are non-taxable; hardware sold with them or non-software services (e.g., advertising, hosting) may still be taxable.
Distractors: D is wrong because 0% applies only to taxable exports; 10% and 5% are not rules for software.

VAT-016.q: Consider the following statements on VAT applicable in 2026:
o: Plant varieties produced and sold by an enterprise are not subject to VAT.
Fertiliser sold is not subject to VAT.
Life insurance services are not subject to VAT.
Goods of a household business with annual revenue of VND 800 million are not subject to VAT.
VAT-016.e: Plant varieties and life insurance are non-taxable; fertiliser is taxed at 5% from 01/7/2025; household businesses with annual revenue of VND 1 billion or less are not subject to VAT from the 2026 tax period.
VAT-016.x:
Basis: Articles 5 and 9 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Law 09/2026/QH16; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: (1) True – plant varieties are non-taxable. (2) False – fertiliser is 5% from 01/07/2025. (3) True – life insurance is non-taxable. (4) True – revenue of 800 million is below the VND 1 billion threshold from the 2026 tax period.

VAT-017.q: Select ALL types of insurance that are not subject to VAT:
VAT-017.e: Life, health and other person-related insurance and livestock/crop insurance are non-taxable; property, fire and vehicle damage insurance are subject to VAT.
VAT-017.x:
Basis: Article 5 of Law 48/2024/QH15 – life, health and learner insurance, other person-related insurance, and livestock, crop and agricultural insurance are not subject to VAT.
Analysis: The test is the insured object: people and agriculture → non-taxable; property and liability → taxable.
Distractors: Fire insurance and motor damage insurance are property insurance and are taxable.

VAT-018.q: An enterprise sells both taxable and non-taxable goods. Input VAT on shared electricity and water invoices that cannot be separately accounted for is:
o: Deductible in proportion to taxable revenue (including revenue not required to be declared) over total revenue
VAT-018.e: Shared input VAT that cannot be separated is deducted by the ratio of taxable revenue (including revenue not required to declare/pay) to total revenue.
VAT-018.x:
Basis: Article 14 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Decree 181/2025/ND-CP – shared input VAT for taxable and non-taxable activities that can't be separately accounted for is credited by revenue ratio.
Working: Creditable = shared input VAT × (taxable revenue, including 'no need to declare and pay' revenue / total revenue); the remainder is expensed.
Distractors: A ignores the non-taxable share; B is too strict; D is wrong because refunds have separate conditions.

VAT-019.q: A Vietnamese company buys consulting services from a foreign organisation without a permanent establishment in Vietnam (not via an e-commerce or digital platform). Who discharges the VAT obligation?
o: The Vietnamese buyer withholds and pays on its behalf
VAT-019.e: An organisation doing business in Vietnam that buys services from a foreign organisation without a PE is the taxpayer under the withhold-and-pay mechanism (commonly called foreign contractor tax).
VAT-019.x:
Basis: Article 4 of Law 48/2024/QH15 – Vietnamese businesses buying services from foreign organisations without a permanent establishment are taxpayers under the withhold-and-pay mechanism (except purchases via e-commerce/digital platforms where the foreign supplier registers directly).
Analysis: This is commonly called foreign contractor tax; the Vietnamese party withholds before payment and declares on the supplier's behalf.
Distractors: A is only right for registered digital platform suppliers; C is wrong because services consumed in Vietnam are taxable; D is wrong as banks withhold only in certain payments to digital platform suppliers.

VAT-020.q: Unprocessed livestock products imported into Vietnam are not subject to VAT at the import stage.
VAT-020.e: True. Article 5(1) exempts them both when sold by the producer and at the import stage.
VAT-020.x:
Basis: Article 5(1) of Law 48/2024/QH15 – unprocessed crop, livestock and aquatic products are non-taxable when sold by producers and at import.
Analysis: True; the subsequent domestic trading stage follows separate rules (5% or 'no need to declare and pay').

VAT-021.q: Match each item with its current VAT treatment:
p: Live beef cattle raised and sold by the farm
VAT-021.e: Self-produced livestock products are non-taxable; animal feed 5%; consulting 10% reduced to 8% under Resolution 204/2025/QH15 (not in the excluded groups); exported services 0%.
VAT-021.x:
Basis: Articles 5 and 9 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Resolution 204/2025/QH15.
Analysis: Live cattle sold by the farm that raised them: unprocessed livestock sold by the producer → non-taxable. Animal feed → 5%. Management consulting consumed in Vietnam → 10%, reduced to 8% until 31/12/2026 as it is not an excluded group. Exported services consumed abroad → 0%.

VAT-022.q: Exported natural resources and minerals that have not been processed into other products are:
VAT-022.e: Unprocessed exported resources and minerals are non-taxable, so 0% does not apply and input VAT is neither deductible nor refundable.
VAT-022.x:
Basis: Article 5 of Law 48/2024/QH15 – exported natural resources and minerals not processed into other products are not subject to VAT.
Analysis: Being non-taxable, the 0% rate doesn't apply and related input VAT can't be credited or refunded – a policy discouraging raw resource exports.
Distractors: 0% applies only to taxable exports; 10% and 5% are wrong.

VAT-023.q: Goods transshipped or in transit through Vietnamese territory are not subject to VAT.
VAT-023.e: True. Goods in transshipment, transit or passing through Vietnam are not subject to VAT.
VAT-023.x:
Basis: Article 5 of Law 48/2024/QH15 – goods in transhipment, transit or passing through Vietnam, and certain temporary import/export goods, are not subject to VAT.
Analysis: True; the goods aren't consumed in Vietnam, so no consumption tax arises.

VAT-024.q: Veterinary services (examination, treatment, disease prevention for animals) are taxed at 10% VAT.
VAT-024.e: False. Medical and veterinary services, including examination, treatment and prevention for humans and animals, are not subject to VAT.
VAT-024.x:
Basis: Article 5 of Law 48/2024/QH15 – medical and veterinary services (examination, treatment and prevention for people and animals) are not subject to VAT.
Analysis: False; veterinary drugs are goods with their own rate, but animal treatment services are non-taxable.

o: Organisations, households and individuals producing/trading taxable goods and services, and organisations/individuals importing taxable goods
Only enterprises with revenue above VND 1 billion
VAT-025.e: VAT payers are organisations, households and individuals producing or trading taxable goods/services and those importing taxable goods (plus withholding cases under Article 4).
VAT-025.x:
Basis: Article 4 of Law 48/2024/QH15.
Analysis: Taxpayers are organisations, households and individuals producing or trading taxable goods and services, and those importing taxable goods, plus withhold-and-pay cases (e.g., buying from foreign suppliers).
Distractors: B confuses this with the credit-method threshold; C confuses the economic bearer (consumers, via prices) with the legal taxpayer; D is wrong because customs only collects import-stage VAT.

VAT-026.q: VAT is a tax on the value added to goods and services arising from production and circulation through to consumption.
VAT-026.e: True. This is the statutory concept of VAT; the tax is borne by the final consumer through the price.
VAT-026.x:
Basis: Article 2 of Law 48/2024/QH15 (definition of VAT).
Analysis: True. VAT is levied on value added at each stage; input crediting avoids cascading, and the final burden passes to the end consumer via prices.

VAT-027.q: Law 09/2026/QH16 does not hard-code the revenue threshold below which household/individual businesses are not subject to VAT; it lets the Government set it from time to time.
VAT-027.e: True. Law 09/2026/QH16 amended Article 5(25) of the VAT Law to delegate the threshold to the Government; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP set it at VND 1 billion.
VAT-027.x:
Basis: Law 09/2026/QH16 amending Article 5(25) of the VAT Law; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Delegating the threshold to the Government allows flexible adjustment without amending the Law; the current level is VND 1 billion/year.

VAT-028.q: The amended VAT, PIT and CIT provisions in Law 09/2026/QH16 apply from:
VAT-028.e: The law took effect on 24/4/2026, but its PIT, VAT and CIT provisions apply from 01/01/2026 to align with the annual tax period.
VAT-028.x:
Basis: Law 09/2026/QH16.
Analysis: The Law took effect on 24/04/2026, but its PIT, VAT and CIT amendments apply from 01/01/2026 to align with the annual tax period.
Distractors: 24/04/2026 is the general effective date, not the tax application date; 01/07/2026 and 01/01/2027 are not in the text.

VAT-029.q: The VAT rates set by the 2024 VAT Law are:
VAT-029.e: The law sets three rates: 0%, 5%, 10%. 8% is a temporary reduction under a National Assembly resolution, not a statutory rate.
VAT-029.x:
Basis: Article 9 of Law 48/2024/QH15 – three rates: 0%, 5%, 10%.
Analysis: 8% is only a temporary 2-point reduction under a National Assembly resolution (Resolution 204/2025/QH15), not a statutory rate.
Distractors: B and D treat 8% as a statutory rate; C includes a non-existent 15%.

VAT-030.q: The VAT reduction (from 10% to 8%) under Resolution 204/2025/QH15 applies until the end of:
VAT-030.e: Resolution 204/2025/QH15 and Decree 174/2025/ND-CP: a 2-point reduction from 01/7/2025 to 31/12/2026.
VAT-030.x:
Basis: Resolution 204/2025/QH15; Decree 174/2025/ND-CP – a 2-point VAT reduction from 01/07/2025 to 31/12/2026.
Analysis: Invoices issued from 01/01/2027 (absent a new policy) revert to 10%; track the invoice date to apply the right rate.
Distractors: The other dates don't match the texts.

VAT-031.q: Select ALL groups of goods/services NOT eligible for the 8% reduced rate:
VAT-031.e: Excluded groups include telecoms, IT, finance, banking, securities, insurance, real estate, metals and prefabricated metal products, mining products (except coal), coke, refined petroleum, chemical products and goods/services subject to special consumption tax (except petrol). F&B and passenger transport are eligible.
VAT-031.x:
Basis: Decree 174/2025/ND-CP – list of goods and services excluded from the reduction.
Analysis: Exclusions are telecoms and IT; finance, banking, securities, insurance; real estate; metals and fabricated metal products; mining products (except coal), coke, refined petroleum, chemicals; and excise-taxed goods/services (except petrol).
Distractors: Food and beverage services and passenger transport aren't excluded, so they get 8%.

VAT-032.q: How does the reduction apply to a business paying VAT by the percentage-of-revenue method?
o: The percentage is cut by 2 points
The percentage used to calculate VAT is reduced by 20%
VAT-032.e: Under Decree 174/2025/ND-CP, businesses using the percentage-of-revenue method get a 20% reduction of the percentage when invoicing eligible goods/services.
VAT-032.x:
Basis: Decree 174/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Businesses using the percentage-of-revenue method get a 20% cut in the percentage, e.g., services 5% → 4%; distribution 1% → 0.8%. The invoice must state the reduction.
Distractors: A applies the 2-point cut of the credit method; C and D have no basis.

VAT-033.q: An enterprise (credit method) provides an eligible service with a pre-tax price of VND 150,000,000 in October 2026. What VAT amount appears on the invoice (VND)?
VAT-033.e: 150,000,000 × 8% = 12,000,000 VND (reduced from 10% to 8% under Resolution 204/2025/QH15 and Decree 174/2025/ND-CP).
VAT-033.x:
Basis: Resolution 204/2025/QH15; Decree 174/2025/ND-CP.
Working: An eligible service invoiced in October 2026 (within the reduction period) → 8%: 150,000,000 × 8% = 12,000,000 VND.
Note: If the service were excluded (e.g., telecoms), it would stay at 10% = 15,000,000 VND.

VAT-034.q: A credit-method enterprise states the 8% rate on the VAT invoice for goods/services eligible for the reduction.
VAT-034.e: True. The invoice must show the 8% rate, the tax amount and the total payable.
VAT-034.x:
Basis: Decree 174/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Credit-method sellers show the 8% rate directly on the VAT invoice; buyers credit the VAT shown.
Note: Invoices with the wrong rate (e.g., 10% on eligible goods) must be adjusted under invoice rules.

VAT-035.q: The VAT reduction applies uniformly at the import, production, processing and trading stages for eligible goods and services.
VAT-035.e: True. The reduction applies uniformly at all those stages.
VAT-035.x:
Basis: Decree 174/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Uniform application at all stages avoids input–output rate mismatches that complicate crediting and refunds.

VAT-036.q: For goods currently taxed at 5% (e.g., animal feed), under the 2025-2026 reduction policy:
VAT-036.e: The 2-point reduction applies only to goods and services taxed at 10%.
VAT-036.x:
Basis: Resolution 204/2025/QH15; Decree 174/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: The policy cuts only goods and services at 10% (excluding listed groups) by 2 points. Animal feed is at 5%, so it isn't eligible.
Distractors: 3% and 4% misread the mechanism; 'exempt' has no basis.

o: Exported goods and services, international transport and other statutory cases
All goods sold to foreigners in Vietnam
Services provided to foreign organisations but consumed in Vietnam
VAT-037.e: 0% applies to exported goods/services (consumed outside Vietnam), international transport and certain other cases; services consumed in Vietnam do not qualify.
VAT-037.x:
Basis: Article 9 of Law 48/2024/QH15 – 0% applies to exported goods and services, international transport and certain statutory cases.
Analysis: The essence of 0% is consumption outside Vietnam (or in non-tariff zones as regulated), so input VAT remains creditable and refundable.
Distractors: B and C are wrong because consumption in Vietnam isn't zero-rated even if the buyer is foreign; D has no basis.

VAT-038.q: Select ALL conditions for exported goods to qualify for 0% under Decree 181/2025/ND-CP:
o: A contract for sale or processing of exported goods
Confirmation from the Ministry of Industry and Trade
VAT-038.e: The conditions are a contract, non-cash payment documents and a customs declaration (with specific exceptions).
VAT-038.x:
Basis: Decree 181/2025/ND-CP – conditions for the 0% rate on exported goods.
Analysis: Three basic conditions: a sale or processing contract; non-cash payment documents; a customs declaration (with some special exceptions).
Distractors: Ministry of Industry and Trade confirmation and bank guarantees are not conditions.

VAT-039.q: Clean water for production and daily use (excluding bottled/jarred water) is taxed at:
VAT-039.e: Clean water for production and daily use is in the 5% group.
VAT-039.x:
Basis: Article 9 of Law 48/2024/QH15 – clean water for production and domestic use is in the 5% group.
Analysis: Bottled water and other beverages aren't in this group and are taxed at 10% (possibly reduced to 8%).
Distractors: 0% is for exports; 'non-taxable' is wrong for clean water.

VAT-040.q: Medicines for disease prevention/treatment and medical equipment are taxed at:
VAT-040.e: Medicines and medical equipment are in the 5% group.
VAT-040.x:
Basis: Article 9 of Law 48/2024/QH15 – medicines and medical equipment are in the 5% group.
Analysis: Distinguish: medical services are non-taxable (VAT-013) while medical goods are taxed at 5%.
Distractors: 10% is standard; 0% is for exports; 'non-taxable' confuses goods with medical services.

VAT-041.q: Agricultural products processed into other products are taxed at 10% (and may qualify for 8% during the reduction period if not in an excluded group).
VAT-041.e: True. Processed agricultural products (and timber, bamboo shoots) are taxed at 10%, reducible to 8% from 01/7/2025 to 31/12/2026 if eligible.
VAT-041.x:
Basis: Article 9 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Decree 174/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Once produce is processed into another product (e.g., roasted coffee, processed meat), it leaves the 5% raw-produce group and takes 10%, reduced to 8% from 01/07/2025 to 31/12/2026 unless excluded.

VAT-042.q: The VAT rate for international transport services is:
VAT-042.x:
Basis: Article 9 of Law 48/2024/QH15 – international transport is zero-rated.
Analysis: It covers carriage of people and goods from Vietnam abroad and from abroad into Vietnam (and domestic legs within the same contract, as regulated).
Distractors: 5% and 10% are domestic rates; 'non-taxable' is wrong since the service is taxable at 0% (with input credit).

VAT-043.q: Services provided to a foreign organisation but consumed in Vietnam still qualify for the 0% rate.
VAT-043.e: False. 0% applies only to services consumed outside Vietnam; services consumed in Vietnam bear the applicable rate (usually 10%).
VAT-043.x:
Basis: Article 9 of Law 48/2024/QH15.
Analysis: False. The 0% test is where the service is consumed, not the buyer's nationality. E.g., hotel services for a foreign company's delegation in Vietnam are taxed at 10% (or 8% during the reduction).

VAT-044.q: Company B trades animal feed (buys and resells to farms). Consider these statements for 2026:
o: Animal feed sold is taxed at 5%.
Input VAT on the feed purchased is deductible if conditions are met.
Unprocessed hay sold by the farmer who grew it is not subject to VAT.
Animal feed currently enjoys a reduction from 5% to 4%.
VAT-044.e: Animal feed is taxed at 5% with deductible input VAT; unprocessed crops sold by the grower are non-taxable; the 2-point reduction applies only to the 10% group.
VAT-044.x:
Basis: Articles 5 and 9 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Decree 174/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: (1) True – animal feed is 5%. (2) True – taxable sales mean input VAT is creditable with valid invoices and non-cash payment. (3) True – unprocessed crops sold by the grower are non-taxable. (4) False – the 2-point reduction applies only to the 10% group.

VAT-045.q: Daily retail sales (VAT-inclusive at 8%) are VND 54,000,000. What is the revenue excluding VAT (VND)?
VAT-045.e: 54,000,000 / 1.08 = 50,000,000 VND; the corresponding VAT is 4,000,000 VND.
VAT-045.x:
Basis: Decree 174/2025/ND-CP (8% rate); separating the VAT base from the gross price.
Working: Net revenue = gross / (1 + rate) = 54,000,000 / 1.08 = 50,000,000 VND; VAT = 4,000,000 VND.
Note: Don't compute 54,000,000 × 8% (4,320,000) – the rate applies to the net, not the gross price.

VAT-046.q: The VAT base for goods sold is:
VAT-046.e: The VAT base is the selling price excluding VAT (including special consumption tax and environmental protection tax, if any).
VAT-046.x:
Basis: Article 7 of Law 48/2024/QH15.
Analysis: The base is the selling price excluding VAT; for goods subject to excise or environmental protection tax, the VAT base includes those taxes.
Distractors: B taxes VAT on itself; C and D are not the tax base.

VAT-047.q: Goods used for promotions in accordance with commercial law have a VAT base of:
o: The selling price of similar goods
VAT-047.e: Goods and services used for promotions under commercial law have a VAT base of zero.
VAT-047.x:
Basis: Article 7 of Law 48/2024/QH15 – goods and services used for promotions under commercial law have a VAT base of zero.
Analysis: The promotion must follow commercial-law procedures (registration/notification). Otherwise, free goods are treated as gifts and taxed at the price of similar goods (VAT-055).
Distractors: The other options apply to gifts or have no basis.

VAT-048.q: The VAT base for goods sold on instalment or deferred payment is:
o: The one-off cash price excluding VAT, excluding instalment/deferred interest
The total amount collected including interest
VAT-048.e: The base is the one-off selling price excluding VAT, without instalment or deferred-payment interest.
VAT-048.x:
Basis: Article 7 of Law 48/2024/QH15.
Analysis: The base is the one-off cash price excluding VAT; instalment interest is financial income, not the goods' price, so it isn't subject to VAT.
Distractors: B includes interest; C and D have no basis.

VAT-049.q: The VAT base for imported goods is:
o: Import value at the border plus import duty, special consumption tax and environmental protection tax (if any)
VAT-049.e: VAT base on imports = customs value + import duty + special consumption tax + environmental protection tax (if any).
VAT-049.x:
Basis: Article 7 of Law 48/2024/QH15.
Formula: Import VAT base = customs value (usually CIF) + import duty (including any additional duties) + excise tax + environmental protection tax.
Distractors: A omits the added taxes; C (FOB) excludes freight and insurance; D is a later-stage selling price.

VAT-050.q: Imported goods have a customs value of VND 400,000,000 and import duty of VND 40,000,000, no SCT or EPT; the item is not eligible for the reduction and the VAT rate is 10%. What is the import VAT (VND)?
VAT-050.x:
Basis: Article 7 of Law 48/2024/QH15.
Working: Base = 400,000,000 + 40,000,000 = 440,000,000 VND; VAT = 440,000,000 × 10% = 44,000,000 VND (an excluded item stays at 10%).
Note: Import VAT paid to customs is creditable as input VAT if conditions are met.

VAT-051.q: The time of determining VAT for a sale of goods is:
o: When ownership or the right to use the goods passes to the buyer, whether or not payment has been received
At the end of the month
VAT-051.e: For goods, VAT arises when ownership or the right to use passes to the buyer, regardless of payment.
VAT-051.x:
Basis: Article 8 of Law 48/2024/QH15.
Analysis: For goods, the tax point is the transfer of ownership or right of use, regardless of payment – also the invoicing time.
Distractors: A (payment) applies only in special cases; C and D have no basis.

VAT-052.q: The time of determining VAT for services is:
o: Completion of the service or invoicing (if earlier), whether or not payment has been received
When the contract liquidation minutes are signed
The last day of the quarter
VAT-052.e: For services, VAT arises on completion of the service or when the invoice is issued, regardless of payment.
VAT-052.x:
Basis: Article 8 of Law 48/2024/QH15.
Analysis: For services, the tax point is completion of the service or invoicing if earlier, regardless of payment.
Distractors: B, C and D don't match the rule; a contract liquidation minute is only a contractual document.

VAT-053.q: Match each activity with its VAT time of determination:
p: Transfer of ownership or right of use
Completion of the service or invoicing (if earlier)
Acceptance and handover of completed work
VAT-053.e: Article 8 of the VAT Law sets the time for each activity; none depends on whether payment has been received.
VAT-053.x:
Basis: Article 8 of Law 48/2024/QH15.
Analysis: Goods – transfer of ownership/use; services – completion or earlier invoicing; imports – customs declaration registration; construction – acceptance and handover of completed work. None depends on payment.

VAT-054.q: Goods moved internally between dependent units to continue production/business are not subject to VAT calculation and payment.
VAT-054.e: True. Internal transfers to continue production/business do not require VAT and no invoice is needed between dependent accounting units.
VAT-054.x:
Basis: Decree 181/2025/ND-CP; Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Internal transfers between dependent units to continue production involve no consumption, so no VAT; internal use for other purposes (gifts, consumption) is still taxable.

VAT-055.q: An enterprise gives goods as gifts to customers (not a promotion under commercial law). The VAT base is:
o: The taxable price of identical or equivalent goods at the time
VAT-055.e: Goods used for exchange, gifts, donations or in lieu of wages are taxed on the price of identical or equivalent goods at that time.
VAT-055.x:
Basis: Article 7 of Law 48/2024/QH15 – goods used for barter, gifts, donations or in lieu of wages are valued at the VAT base of similar goods at that time.
Analysis: Unlike a lawful promotion (zero base), gifts outside a promotion still bear output VAT.
Distractors: A confuses it with promotion; C cost isn't the base; D is wrong as VAT is due.

VAT-056.q: For real-estate business, the VAT base is:
o: The transfer price minus the deductible land price
VAT-056.e: The VAT base for real estate is the transfer price less the land price deductible for VAT.
VAT-056.x:
Basis: Article 7 of Law 48/2024/QH15.
Analysis: For property: base = transfer price − deductible land price (land use rights are non-taxable – VAT-012).
Distractors: B taxes land; C taxes only land, the reverse; D budget cost isn't the selling price.

VAT-057.q: An enterprise sells a generator on instalment: one-off price excluding VAT VND 900 million, total instalment amount (excluding VAT) VND 960 million. The VAT base is:
VAT-057.e: The base is the one-off price excluding VAT (900 million); the 60 million difference is instalment interest and not part of the VAT base.
VAT-057.x:
Basis: Article 7 of Law 48/2024/QH15.
Working: Base = one-off cash price excluding VAT = 900 million; the 60 million difference (960 − 900) is instalment interest, not subject to VAT.
Distractors: B includes interest; C is only the interest; D has no basis.

VAT-058.q: For construction and installation, VAT is determined at acceptance and handover of the completed work or volume, regardless of payment.
VAT-058.e: True. This is the timing rule for construction and installation.
VAT-058.x:
Basis: Article 8 of Law 48/2024/QH15.
Analysis: True. Construction contracts are often paid by milestones, but the tax point is acceptance and handover of completed work – even if the owner hasn't paid.

VAT-059.q: The credit (deduction) method is mandatory for businesses (other than household/individual businesses) with annual revenue from goods and services of at least:
VAT-059.e: Businesses with annual revenue of VND 1 billion or more apply the credit method; those below may register voluntarily.
VAT-059.x:
Basis: Article 12 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Businesses (other than household/individual businesses) with annual revenue of VND 1 billion or more must use the credit method; below that they may opt in.
Distractors: 500 million, 3 billion and 50 billion relate to other rules (household businesses, monthly filing…).

VAT-060.q: Match each activity group with its VAT percentage under the direct method on revenue:
p: Production, transport, goods-related services, construction with materials
VAT-060.e: VAT percentages on revenue: goods distribution 1%; services and construction without materials 5%; production, transport, goods-related services and construction with materials 3%; other activities 2%.
VAT-060.x:
Basis: Article 13 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: The rates reflect average value added by group: distribution 1% (low value added); production, transport, goods-related services and construction including materials 3%; services and construction excluding materials 5% (high value added); other activities 2%.

VAT-061.q: A small company using the direct method has quarterly revenue from distributing goods of VND 600,000,000 (not eligible for the reduction). What VAT is payable (VND)?
VAT-061.x:
Basis: Article 13 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Working: VAT = 600,000,000 × 1% = 6,000,000 VND (distribution of goods, not eligible for the 20% reduction).

VAT-062.q: A service company using the direct method has Q3/2026 consulting revenue of VND 400,000,000, eligible for the reduction under Decree 174/2025/ND-CP. What VAT is payable (VND)?
VAT-062.e: The 5% service percentage is cut by 20% to 4%: 400,000,000 × 5% × 80% = 16,000,000 VND.
VAT-062.x:
Basis: Law 48/2024/QH15; Decree 174/2025/ND-CP.
Working: The 5% service rate cut by 20% becomes 4%: 400,000,000 × 4% = 16,000,000 VND.
Note: Without the reduction it would be 20,000,000 VND.

VAT-063.q: The direct method on value added applies to:
o: Trading and crafting of gold, silver and gemstones
VAT-063.e: VAT payable = value added × rate, applied to trading and crafting of gold, silver and gemstones.
VAT-063.x:
Basis: Article 13 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: The direct value-added method (VAT = (selling − buying price) × rate) applies only to trading and crafting gold, silver and gemstones.
Distractors: Household businesses use percentage of revenue; exporters use the credit method; most financial services are non-taxable.

VAT-064.q: VAT payable under the credit method equals:
o: Output VAT minus deductible input VAT
VAT-064.e: Credit method: VAT payable = output VAT − deductible input VAT.
VAT-064.x:
Basis: Article 12 of Law 48/2024/QH15.
Formula: VAT payable = output VAT − creditable input VAT (inputs must meet invoice and payment conditions).
Distractors: B is the percentage-of-revenue method; C is the direct value-added method; D reverses the formula.

VAT-065.q: In September 2026 an enterprise has output VAT of VND 180,000,000, deductible input VAT of VND 125,000,000 and VND 20,000,000 of unused credit brought forward. What VAT is payable for the period (VND)?
VAT-065.x:
Basis: Article 12 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Working: 180,000,000 − 125,000,000 − 20,000,000 (brought forward) = 35,000,000 VND payable.
Note: A negative result is carried forward (or refunded if eligible).

VAT-066.q: A newly established enterprise expecting revenue below VND 1 billion may still voluntarily register for the credit method.
VAT-066.e: True. Businesses (other than household/individual businesses) may register voluntarily for the credit method.
VAT-066.x:
Basis: Article 12 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Enterprises (other than household/individual businesses) may opt into the credit method below VND 1 billion – often beneficial with many taxable inputs or customers needing VAT invoices.

VAT-067.q: A household business with revenue above VND 1 billion/year may choose to pay VAT by the credit method like an enterprise.
VAT-067.e: False. Household/individual businesses above the threshold pay VAT by the direct method as a percentage of revenue.
VAT-067.x:
Basis: Law 48/2024/QH15; Decree 68/2026/ND-CP (amended by Decree 141/2026/ND-CP).
Analysis: False. Household and individual businesses above the threshold pay VAT as a percentage of revenue; to use the credit method they must convert to an enterprise.

VAT-068.q: Arrange the steps to determine VAT payable under the credit method in a period:
o: Determine revenue and output VAT from invoices issued
Collect input invoices and check deduction conditions (invoice, non-cash payment)
Allocate shared input VAT between taxable and non-taxable activities
Determine VAT payable or credit carried forward
VAT-068.e: Sequence: output → eligible input → allocate shared input → offset prior credit → payable or carry-forward.
VAT-068.x:
Basis: Articles 12 and 14 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Sequence: (1) output VAT per issued invoices; (2) collect inputs and check credit conditions; (3) apportion shared inputs; (4) offset prior-period credits; (5) determine payable or carry-forward.
Note: Step (2) causes most audit findings (invalid invoices, missing payment documents).

VAT-069.q: Can a taxpayer using the direct percentage-of-revenue method deduct input VAT?
o: No; input VAT is included in cost
VAT-069.e: The direct method does not allow input VAT deduction; VAT paid on purchases is included in historical cost, cost of sales or expenses.
VAT-069.x:
Basis: Article 13 of Law 48/2024/QH15.
Analysis: Under the direct method, input VAT isn't credited; it's included in asset cost, COGS or expenses.
Distractors: B, C and D allow crediting, which the direct method doesn't.

VAT-070.q: From 01/7/2025, to deduct input VAT, purchases (including imports) must have non-cash payment documents when their value (VAT-inclusive) is at least:
VAT-070.e: Article 26 of Decree 181/2025/ND-CP lowered the threshold from VND 20 million to VND 5 million.
VAT-070.x:
Basis: Article 14 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Article 26 of Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: From 01/07/2025, the non-cash payment threshold for crediting input VAT fell from 20 million to 5 million VND (VAT-inclusive).
Distractors: 20 million was the old threshold; 10 and 50 million have no basis.
Note: The threshold applies per purchase (invoice value).

VAT-071.q: A buyer depositing cash into the seller's bank account counts as a non-cash payment document for VAT deduction.
VAT-071.e: False. Decree 181/2025/ND-CP excludes cash deposited by the buyer into the seller's account.
VAT-071.x:
Basis: Article 14 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Article 26 of Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: False. A buyer depositing cash into the seller's account is excluded, because the buyer still pays in cash and the flow can't be traced from the buyer's account.

VAT-072.q: Select ALL documents accepted as non-cash payment documents for VAT deduction:
o: Payment orders/debit advices transferring from the buyer's account to the seller's account
Card or e-wallet payment records under non-cash payment rules
A slip for cash deposited by the buyer into the seller's account
A cash payment voucher signed by both parties
VAT-072.e: Non-cash payment documents follow Decree 52/2024/ND-CP, except cash deposited by the buyer into the seller's account; cash vouchers do not qualify.
VAT-072.x:
Basis: Article 26 of Decree 181/2025/ND-CP; Decree 52/2024/ND-CP on non-cash payments.
Analysis: Valid: payment orders and debit advices from the buyer's to the seller's account; card and e-wallet payments as regulated. Invalid: cash deposits into the seller's account; cash payment vouchers.

VAT-073.q: A deferred purchase of VND 60 million (VAT-inclusive) reaches its contractual due date but the enterprise has no non-cash payment document. The enterprise must:
o: Do nothing as it has already declared
Reduce the deducted input VAT in the period when payment falls due under the contract
Reduce it in the period the invoice was declared
VAT-073.e: Article 26 of Decree 181/2025/ND-CP: if there is no non-cash payment document at the due date, reduce input VAT in the period the payment obligation arises; once the document is available, it may be re-deducted.
VAT-073.x:
Basis: Article 26 of Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Deferred-payment purchases are credited before payment; if no non-cash proof exists by the contractual due date, input VAT must be reduced in the period the payment fell due, and re-credited once proof exists.
Distractors: A ignores the reversal duty; C uses the wrong period; D has no basis.

VAT-074.q: Before the contractual payment date, an enterprise may still deduct input VAT on deferred purchases even without a non-cash payment document.
VAT-074.e: True. Where no document exists because payment is not yet due under the contract, deduction is still allowed.
VAT-074.x:
Basis: Article 26 of Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Input VAT can be credited on a valid invoice as long as the contractual payment date hasn't arrived; keep the contract showing the payment terms.

VAT-075.q: An employee authorised by the company pays VND 8 million with a personal card; the company later reimburses the employee by bank transfer. The input VAT is:
o: Not deductible because an individual paid
Deductible if there is a financial/internal regulation on authorisation and the company reimburses the employee by non-cash means
Deductible even if reimbursed in cash
VAT-075.e: Decree 181/2025/ND-CP adds the case where an employee is authorised to pay non-cash under internal rules and the company reimburses the employee non-cash.
VAT-075.x:
Basis: Article 26 of Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Decree 181/2025 allows employees authorised to pay by non-cash means (personal cards), provided a financial or internal policy covers the authorisation and the company reimburses the employee by non-cash means.
Distractors: A is too strict; C has no basis; D is wrong because cash reimbursement breaks the non-cash chain.

VAT-076.q: Select ALL conditions to deduct input VAT on domestic goods worth VND 30 million:
o: The goods are used for VAT-taxable activities
The seller has fully paid VAT on that invoice
VAT-076.e: Conditions are a legitimate invoice, a non-cash payment document (from VND 5 million) and use for taxable activities. The seller having declared/paid is not a deduction condition; the similar refund condition was abolished from 01/01/2026.
VAT-076.x:
Basis: Article 14 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Article 26 of Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: A 30 million purchase exceeds the 5 million threshold, so three conditions apply: (A) a lawful VAT invoice; (B) non-cash payment documents; (C) use for taxable activities (or 'no need to declare and pay' activities).
Distractors: (D) The seller having paid the tax is not a credit condition – the buyer can't control it; the similar refund condition was repealed from 01/01/2026 by Law 149/2025. (E) There is no tax-authority confirmation before crediting – taxpayers self-assess.

VAT-077.q: Input VAT on goods/services used for selling unprocessed agricultural products between enterprises (where no output VAT is declared) is still deductible.
VAT-077.e: True. Law 149/2025/QH15 provides no declaration/payment for such sales, but input VAT is deductible.
VAT-077.x:
Basis: Law 149/2025/QH15 amending Article 5(1) of the VAT Law.
Analysis: True. The core difference between 'no need to declare and pay' and 'non-taxable': the former still allows input credit (its revenue goes in the numerator when apportioning shared inputs), the latter doesn't.
Note: When apportioning shared inputs, don't classify business-to-business raw produce sales as non-taxable – that error cuts the creditable amount.

VAT-078.q: A purchase invoice of VND 4.8 million (VAT-inclusive) is paid in cash. The input VAT:
o: Is deductible if other conditions are met, as it is below the VND 5 million threshold
VAT-078.e: Non-cash payment is mandatory only from VND 5 million; the 4.8 million purchase is not caught.
VAT-078.x:
Basis: Article 14 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Article 26 of Decree 181/2025/ND-CP – non-cash payment is required for purchases of 5 million VND or more (VAT-inclusive).
Analysis: 4.8 million < 5 million, so cash is allowed; input VAT is creditable with a lawful invoice and taxable use.
Distractors: A misapplies the threshold; C has no basis; D – Form 01/TNDN is for purchases without invoices, irrelevant here.
Note: Splitting invoices to avoid the threshold is a red flag (see VAT-119).

VAT-079.q: An enterprise finds a legitimate input invoice that was omitted from its returns. It may:
o: Declare and deduct it additionally before the tax authority announces an inspection/audit decision at its premises
VAT-079.e: Omitted input invoices may be declared and deducted additionally before the tax authority announces an inspection or audit decision.
VAT-079.x:
Basis: Article 14 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Article 26 of Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: A missed lawful input invoice may be declared and credited by supplementary filing, provided this happens before the authority announces an on-site inspection decision. After that, supplementary filings that increase credits are restricted.
Distractors: A is too strict; C removes the credit without basis; D – refunds are a separate procedure with their own conditions.

VAT-080.q: Input VAT that has been deducted cannot also be included in deductible expenses for CIT.
VAT-080.e: True. Deducted input VAT is not a cost of the enterprise.
VAT-080.x:
Basis: Law 48/2024/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP (CIT deductible expenses).
Analysis: True. Credited input VAT is offset against output VAT – the business recovers it, so it isn't an expense. Only non-creditable input VAT (e.g., the car portion above 1.6 billion, the share for non-taxable activities) goes to expense or asset cost.
Note: Double counting (credited and expensed) is a common review finding.

VAT-081.q: Input VAT on goods/services used only for non-taxable activities is not deductible.
VAT-081.e: True. Input VAT is deductible only for goods/services used for taxable activities (and the statutory 'no declaration' cases).
VAT-081.x:
Basis: Article 14 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Article 26 of Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Matching principle: only input VAT on supplies used for activities with output VAT (including 0%) and statutory 'no need to declare and pay' activities is creditable. Input VAT used solely for non-taxable activities is expensed or capitalised.

VAT-082.q: An enterprise sells both taxable and non-taxable goods. A shared electricity invoice carries VAT of VND 50,000,000. Revenue in the period: taxable VND 7 billion, non-taxable VND 3 billion. How much input VAT is deductible (VND)?
VAT-082.e: 50,000,000 × 7 / (7 + 3) = 35,000,000 VND; the remaining 15,000,000 VND is expensed.
VAT-082.x:
Basis: Article 14 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Article 26 of Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Working: Taxable revenue ratio = 7 / (7 + 3) = 70%. Creditable VAT = 50,000,000 × 70% = 35,000,000 VND; the remaining 15,000,000 VND is expensed.
Note: The ratio is provisional per filing period and finalised annually; adjust any difference at year-end.

VAT-083.q: A credit-method enterprise buys animal feed at a pre-tax price of VND 200,000,000, rate 5%, paid by bank transfer and used for taxable activities. How much input VAT is deductible (VND)?
VAT-083.x:
Basis: Articles 9 and 14 of Law 48/2024/QH15.
Working: Animal feed is 5% (not eligible for the 2-point cut): 200,000,000 × 5% = 10,000,000 VND. With an invoice, bank transfer and taxable use, it's fully creditable.
Note: Before 01/07/2025, animal feed was non-taxable, so no such credit arose.

VAT-084.q: Under Decree 181/2025/ND-CP, the minimum uncredited input VAT for a refund claim for investment projects and exports is:
VAT-084.e: Refunds apply when uncredited input VAT is VND 300 million or more (plus other conditions).
VAT-084.x:
Basis: Article 15 of Law 48/2024/QH15 (amended by Law 149/2025/QH15); Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: The 300 million refund threshold applies to investment projects, exports and producers of 5%-rated goods. Below it, the balance is carried forward.
Distractors: 100, 200 and 500 million aren't statutory thresholds.

VAT-085.q: A business producing only goods taxed at 5% is entitled to a VAT refund when:
o: After 12 consecutive months or 4 consecutive quarters with uncredited input VAT of VND 300 million or more
It is not eligible for refunds
VAT-085.e: This new refund case in the 2024 VAT Law prevents producers of 5% goods (animal feed, fertiliser) from having input VAT locked up.
VAT-085.x:
Basis: Article 15 of Law 48/2024/QH15 (amended by Law 149/2025/QH15); Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Producers of only 5%-rated goods (feed, fertiliser, farm machinery…) often have 10% inputs exceeding 5% outputs, trapping VAT. The 2024 Law allows a refund when 300 million or more remains uncredited after 12 consecutive months or 4 quarters.
Distractors: B ignores the threshold; C has the wrong period; D is wrong as this is the new refund case.

VAT-086.q: Production of goods/services taxed at 5% qualifies for refund of uncredited input VAT arising from 01/7/2025.
VAT-086.e: True. The transitional rule in Decree 181/2025/ND-CP applies to amounts arising from 01/7/2025.
VAT-086.x:
Basis: Article 15 of Law 48/2024/QH15; transitional provisions of Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. As Law 48/2024 took effect on 01/07/2025, the uncredited input VAT considered for this refund counts from amounts arising on or after that date; earlier balances continue to be carried forward.

VAT-087.q: From 01/01/2026, the refund condition requiring the seller to have declared and paid VAT on the invoices claimed by the buyer has been abolished.
VAT-087.e: True. Law 149/2025/QH15 repealed Article 15(9)(c) of the 2024 VAT Law.
VAT-087.x:
Basis: Law 149/2025/QH15 repealing Article 15(9)(c) of Law 48/2024/QH15.
Analysis: True. The 'seller must have declared and paid' condition was criticised because buyers can't control sellers' compliance, causing refund bottlenecks. From 01/01/2026 it was repealed; seller-side invoice risks are handled by post-audit and the seller's own liability.

VAT-088.q: Select ALL cases eligible for a VAT refund:
o: An investment project with uncredited input VAT of VND 300 million or more meeting the conditions
Exported goods/services with uncredited input VAT reaching the threshold
A producer of 5% goods with uncredited input VAT of VND 300 million or more after 12 months or 4 consecutive quarters
A domestic seller of 10% goods with uncredited input VAT of VND 30 million
Foreigners buying goods in Vietnam and taking them out on departure
VAT-088.e: Domestic sales at 10% with uncredited input VAT carry the credit forward; they are not refundable.
VAT-088.x:
Basis: Article 15 of Law 48/2024/QH15 (amended by Law 149/2025/QH15); Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Refund cases: (A) eligible investment projects with 300 million or more; (B) exports meeting the threshold; (C) 5%-rated producers after 12 months/4 quarters; (E) foreigners taking goods out when departing.
Distractors: (D) Domestic 10% sales with excess input VAT are only carried forward – no refund case, and 30 million is below every threshold.

VAT-089.q: Uncredited input VAT that does not qualify for a refund is carried forward to the next period.
VAT-089.e: True. The remaining credit is carried forward.
VAT-089.x:
Basis: Article 15 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Excess input VAT is not lost but carried forward without time limit; a refund is claimed only when a refund case, threshold and conditions are met.

VAT-090.q: A foreigner holding a foreign passport who buys goods in Vietnam and takes them out on departure is entitled to:
VAT-090.e: This is the VAT refund scheme for foreigners carrying goods out on departure (subject to conditions and procedures).
VAT-090.x:
Basis: Article 15 of Law 48/2024/QH15 (amended by Law 149/2025/QH15); Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Foreigners (foreign passport holders) buying at participating stores and carrying goods out through border gates with refund points get VAT refunds under the prescribed conditions – the goods are consumed outside Vietnam.
Distractors: B confuses it with import duty; C and D have no basis.

VAT-091.q: An investment project that started before 01/7/2025 and is still in its investment phase at 01/7/2025:
o: Applies the investment-project refund rules of Decree 181/2025/ND-CP
Continues fully under the old rules until completion
VAT-091.e: Transitional rule of Decree 181/2025/ND-CP: projects still in the investment phase at 01/7/2025 apply the new refund rules.
VAT-091.x:
Basis: Article 15 of Law 48/2024/QH15; transitional provisions of Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Projects started before 01/07/2025 but still in the investment phase on that date apply Decree 181/2025's project refund rules to claims from then on.
Distractors: B denies refunds; C contradicts applying the new rules to the remaining period; D has no basis.

VAT-092.q: A crop-growing enterprise (credit method) has the following 2026 transactions. Consider the statements:
o: Self-grown fresh fruit and vegetables sold to a processor are not subject to VAT.
Input VAT on fertiliser used solely for the vegetable farm is always fully deductible even though output is non-taxable.
Seedlings bought for new planting are not subject to VAT at purchase.
Outsourced agricultural harvesting services are not subject to VAT.
VAT-092.e: Self-produced farm products are non-taxable; input VAT for non-taxable activities is not deductible (allocate if shared); plant varieties and harvesting services are non-taxable.
VAT-092.x:
Basis: Articles 5 and 14 of Law 48/2024/QH15 (amended by Law 149/2025/QH15); Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: (1) True – self-grown fresh produce is non-taxable. (2) False – fertiliser used solely for non-taxable output isn't creditable and is expensed; shared use must be apportioned. (3) True – plant varieties are non-taxable at all stages. (4) True – agricultural services such as ploughing, irrigation and harvesting fall under Article 5.

VAT-093.q: Match each transaction of a diversified agricultural enterprise with its VAT treatment:
p: Selling self-grown fresh produce to a plant
Not subject to VAT (self-produced farm product)
VAT-093.e: Self-produced farm products and plant varieties are non-taxable; animal feed 5%; transport services 10% reduced to 8% under Resolution 204/2025/QH15.
VAT-093.x:
Basis: Articles 5 and 9 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Resolution 204/2025/QH15.
Analysis: Self-grown produce – non-taxable. Self-mixed animal feed – 5% group (no reduction). Seedlings – plant varieties, non-taxable. Transport service – 10%, reduced to 8% until 31/12/2026.
Note: A business with revenue streams under different regimes must apportion shared input VAT (VAT-082).

VAT-094.q: Assets contributed as capital to another enterprise (with valuation minutes and valid contribution records) are not subject to VAT declaration and payment.
VAT-094.e: True. Capital contribution in kind is a 'no declaration' case and also requires no invoice.
VAT-094.x:
Basis: Decree 181/2025/ND-CP (cases with no need to declare and pay VAT); Decree 254/2026/ND-CP on invoices.
Analysis: True. Contributing assets as capital exchanges assets for equity, not a sale for consumption; documents include the contribution minute, valuation minute and JV contract/charter. The recipient records the agreed value.
Note: Where input VAT on the asset was credited, check any adjustment guidance and keep full documentation.

VAT-095.q: Select ALL receipts that do NOT require VAT declaration and payment:
o: Compensation, bonuses and support not linked to sales of goods/services
Capital contribution in kind to another enterprise
Collections/payments on behalf of others not linked to own sales
Sales of goods to domestic customers
VAT-095.e: Compensation/bonuses/support not linked to sales, capital contribution in kind and collections/payments on behalf are not declared. Scrap and domestic sales are taxable.
VAT-095.x:
Basis: Decree 181/2025/ND-CP (cases with no need to declare and pay VAT).
Analysis: (A) Compensation, bonuses and support not tied to sales – not declared. (B) Asset contributions – not declared. (D) Collections and payments on behalf of others not tied to own sales (e.g., collecting utility bills as agent) – not declared.
Distractors: (C) Scrap sales are sales of goods and bear VAT; (E) domestic sales are obviously taxable.
Note: 'Support' tied to purchase conditions (volume targets) is in substance a discount and must go through adjustment invoices.

VAT-096.q: An enterprise issued an invoice at 10% for goods eligible for the 8% rate. The correct treatment is:
o: Leave it, since overpaying is not a violation
Issue an adjustment or replacement invoice under e-invoice rules
Cancel the invoice and issue a new one
VAT-096.e: E-invoices with a wrong rate are corrected by adjustment or replacement invoices; cancellation is no longer a procedure.
VAT-096.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP on invoices; Decree 174/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: An e-invoice sent with the wrong rate is corrected by an adjustment or replacement invoice (with buyer agreement if needed). Both parties declare per the corrected invoice.
Distractors: A is wrong as the wrong rate misstates the buyer's input VAT and breaches invoicing rules; C – cancelling sent e-invoices is no longer available; D has no legal effect.

VAT-097.q: Exported goods that fail the non-cash payment document condition:
o: Do not qualify for 0% and are declared as domestic sales
VAT-097.e: Exports that fail the 0% conditions are declared and taxed like domestic sales.
VAT-097.x:
Basis: Law 48/2024/QH15 (amended by Law 149/2025/QH15); Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Non-cash payment proof is a mandatory 0% condition. Without it, the goods are treated as domestic sales and taxed at the domestic rate (e.g., 10%, or 8% if reduced), with no export refund.
Distractors: A ignores the condition; C and D have no basis.

VAT-098.q: The usual VAT filing period for an enterprise is:
VAT-098.e: VAT is filed monthly or quarterly; the taxpayer determines which applies under the rules.
VAT-098.x:
Basis: Tax Administration Law 108/2025/QH15; Decree 252/2026/ND-CP; Circular 89/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: VAT is filed monthly or quarterly. Quarterly filing typically applies to taxpayers meeting the prior-year revenue criteria or newly operating; others file monthly. Taxpayers self-determine and notify changes per guidance.
Distractors: B confuses it with annual CIT finalisation; C and D are per-transaction filing used only in special cases (e.g., foreign contractors).

VAT-099.q: An enterprise receives a 30% advance on a goods sale contract; the goods have not been delivered. The VAT time of determination for this sale of goods is:
o: When ownership or the right to use the goods is transferred
VAT-099.e: For goods, VAT arises on transfer of ownership or the right to use, regardless of payment.
VAT-099.x:
Basis: Article 8 of Law 48/2024/QH15 (amended by Law 149/2025/QH15); Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: For goods, an advance doesn't trigger the tax point; VAT arises on transfer of ownership or right of use. The 30% advance is recorded as a customer prepayment.
Distractors: A applies only to certain services with specific advance rules; C and D have no basis.
Note: For services, if an invoice is issued on receipt of an advance, the tax point is the invoice date.

VAT-100.q: An enterprise sells goods with a trade discount shown on the invoice. The VAT base is:
VAT-100.e: Where a trade discount is given, the VAT base is the discounted price.
VAT-100.x:
Basis: Article 7 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: A trade discount shown on the invoice reduces the actual price, so the base is the net price. If the discount is determined later (cumulative volume), issue a downward adjustment invoice.
Distractors: B taxes money never received; C and D aren't the tax base.

VAT-101.q: A credit-method enterprise sells eligible goods with a list price of VND 120,000,000 excluding VAT and a 10% trade discount shown on the invoice. What is the output VAT (VND)?
VAT-101.x:
Basis: Article 7 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Decree 174/2025/ND-CP.
Working: Net price = 120,000,000 × (1 − 10%) = 108,000,000 VND. VAT (8%) = 108,000,000 × 8% = 8,640,000 VND.
Note: 120,000,000 × 8% = 9,600,000 is wrong because it ignores the invoiced discount.

VAT-102.q: The VAT base for processing (toll manufacturing) is:
o: The processing fee excluding VAT, including labour, fuel, power, auxiliary materials and other processing costs
The value of materials received for processing
VAT-102.e: For processing, the base is the contractual processing fee excluding VAT, including costs serving the processing.
VAT-102.x:
Basis: Article 7 of Law 48/2024/QH15.
Analysis: The processor doesn't own the main materials, so the base is the contract processing fee excluding VAT, including labour, fuel, power, auxiliary materials and other costs borne by the processor.
Distractors: B and C include materials owned by the principal; D is wrong as processing is taxable.

VAT-103.q: The VAT base for leasing assets is:
o: The rent excluding VAT; where several periods are prepaid, the total prepaid amount
The net book value of the asset
The purchase price of the asset
VAT-103.e: The base is the rent excluding VAT; if rent for several periods is collected in advance, VAT is on the total prepaid amount.
VAT-103.x:
Basis: Article 7 of Law 48/2024/QH15.
Analysis: The base for leasing is the rent excluding VAT. If several periods are prepaid, VAT is on the total prepaid at receipt (unlike accounting, which spreads revenue – see VAT-134).
Distractors: B and C use asset values instead of the service price; D is only part of revenue.

VAT-104.q: Under Official Letter 7451/CT-QLNT (07/10/2026), for purchases used for both VAT-taxable and non-taxable activities:
VAT-104.e: The Tax Department restated the principle: shared input VAT is deductible only for the portion attributable to taxable activities; if it cannot be separated, allocate by the revenue ratio.
o: Only the input VAT attributable to taxable activities is deductible
All of it is deductible if taxable revenue is larger
VAT-104.x:
Basis: Tax Department Official Letter 7451/CT-QLNT of 07/10/2026; Article 14 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: The letter restates the matching principle: shared input VAT is creditable only for the taxable share; separate accounting first, otherwise apportion by revenue.
Distractors: B is wrong as a larger taxable share doesn't make the non-taxable part creditable; C is too strict; D has no basis.

VAT-105.q: Under Official Letter 7451/CT-QLNT (07/10/2026), a business that received a VAT refund but later ceases operations without generating output VAT from its main business must repay the refunded amount.
VAT-105.e: True. A refund presumes future taxable revenue; if operations cease with no output from the main business, the refund must be repaid.
VAT-105.x:
Basis: Official Letter 7451/CT-QLNT of 07/10/2026.
Analysis: True. Refunds (especially for projects) assume future taxable revenue; if the business ceases without output from its main activity, the basis disappears and refunded VAT must be repaid.
Note: Assess this risk when deciding to close a project early.

VAT-106.q: Under Official Letter 7451/CT-QLNT, when a business sells a VAT-taxable asset it must reduce the input VAT previously deducted on that asset.
VAT-106.e: False. When the asset sale itself bears output VAT, the previously deducted input VAT on the asset is not adjusted.
VAT-106.x:
Basis: Official Letter 7451/CT-QLNT of 07/10/2026.
Analysis: False. When an asset is sold with output VAT, it stays in the taxable chain, so credited input VAT stands. Reversal arises only if the asset shifts to non-taxable use or in specific prescribed cases.

VAT-107.q: Under Official Letter 7634/CT-QLNT (14/10/2026), how are international transport support services (handling, customs clearance, packing…) performed abroad and not consumed in Vietnam treated?
VAT-107.e: Services performed and consumed outside Vietnam fall outside the VAT Law; the business must still issue an invoice to the buyer under Article 4(1) of Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
o: Outside the scope of the VAT Law, but an invoice must still be issued
No invoice needed because no VAT applies
VAT-107.x:
Basis: Official Letter 7634/CT-QLNT of 14/10/2026; Article 4(1) of Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Services performed and consumed entirely abroad involve no consumption in Vietnam, so they fall outside the VAT Law – not 0% (which requires a taxable supply meeting export conditions). The invoicing obligation still applies.
Distractors: B confuses it with exported services; C applies domestic VAT; D is wrong as invoicing is independent of tax liability.

VAT-108.q: An enterprise has both taxable and non-taxable sales. Input VAT on a shared office lease is VND 24,000,000. Period revenue: taxable VND 4.5 billion; non-taxable VND 1.5 billion. How much input VAT is deductible (VND)?
VAT-108.e: 24,000,000 × 4.5 / 6 = 18,000,000 VND; the remaining 6,000,000 VND is expensed.
VAT-108.x:
Basis: Article 14 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Decree 181/2025/ND-CP; Official Letter 7451/CT-QLNT.
Working: Ratio = 4.5 / (4.5 + 1.5) = 75%. Creditable = 24,000,000 × 75% = 18,000,000 VND; 6,000,000 VND is expensed.

VAT-109.q: In October 2026 a credit-method enterprise has output VAT of VND 96,000,000 and deductible input VAT of VND 132,000,000. How much credit is carried forward (VND)?
VAT-109.e: 132,000,000 − 96,000,000 = 36,000,000 VND carried forward (if not eligible for a refund).
VAT-109.x:
Basis: Articles 12 and 15 of Law 48/2024/QH15.
Working: Output 96,000,000 − input 132,000,000 = −36,000,000 VND → nothing payable; 36,000,000 VND is carried forward (below the 300 million threshold and not a refund case).

VAT-110.q: An importer brings in spirits: customs value VND 200,000,000, import duty VND 50,000,000, special consumption tax VND 162,500,000; VAT rate 10% (SCT goods are excluded from the reduction). What is the import VAT (VND)?
VAT-110.x:
Basis: Article 7 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Decree 174/2025/ND-CP (excise goods aren't reduced).
Working: VAT base = 200,000,000 + 50,000,000 + 162,500,000 = 412,500,000 VND; VAT = 412,500,000 × 10% = 41,250,000 VND.
Note: Omitting excise from the base (250,000,000 × 10% = 25,000,000) is a common error.

VAT-111.q: A restaurant (credit method) collects VND 5,400,000 for a party, inclusive of 8% VAT (eligible for the reduction). What is the output VAT (VND)?
VAT-111.x:
Basis: Resolution 204/2025/QH15; Decree 174/2025/ND-CP – food and beverage services reduced to 8%.
Working: Net = 5,400,000 / 1.08 = 5,000,000 VND; VAT = 400,000 VND.
Note: 5,400,000 × 8% = 432,000 is wrong – the rate was applied to the gross price.

VAT-112.q: A construction company on the direct method has Q3/2026 revenue from construction including materials of VND 800,000,000, eligible for the reduction. What VAT is payable (VND)?
VAT-112.e: The 3% percentage is reduced by 20% to 2.4%: 800,000,000 × 3% × 80% = 19,200,000 VND.
VAT-112.x:
Basis: Article 13 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Decree 174/2025/ND-CP.
Working: Construction including materials – 3%; cut by 20% → 2.4%. VAT = 800,000,000 × 2.4% = 19,200,000 VND.
Note: Construction excluding materials uses 5% (reduced to 4%).

VAT-113.q: An enterprise uses its own products to pay employees in lieu of wages. The VAT base is:
VAT-113.e: Goods used for exchange, gifts or in lieu of wages are taxed on the price of identical or equivalent goods at the time.
o: The taxable price of identical or equivalent products at the time
VAT-113.x:
Basis: Article 7 of Law 48/2024/QH15.
Analysis: Paying wages in products is consumption – employees receive goods instead of cash – so output VAT applies at the price of similar goods at the time, with revenue and taxable employee income recognised.
Distractors: B is for lawful promotions only; C cost isn't the base; D is wrong as VAT arises.

VAT-114.q: Goods/services used for promotions that do not comply with commercial law still have a VAT base of zero.
VAT-114.e: False. Only promotions conducted in accordance with commercial law have a zero VAT base; otherwise they are taxed like gifts.
VAT-114.x:
Basis: Article 7 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Commercial Law and decrees on promotions.
Analysis: False. A zero base applies only to promotions that comply with commercial law (notification/registration, value limits…). Otherwise, free goods are treated as gifts and taxed at the price of similar goods.

VAT-115.q: Select ALL goods/services NOT subject to VAT:
VAT-115.e: Credit services, capital transfers, teaching/vocational training and software are non-taxable; tax consulting is taxed at 10%.
o: Teaching and vocational training under the law
VAT-115.x:
Basis: Article 5 of Law 48/2024/QH15.
Analysis: (A) Credit services, (B) capital transfers, (C) teaching and vocational training and (E) computer software are all listed as non-taxable in Article 5.
Distractors: (D) Tax advice is a professional service taxed at 10% (reduced to 8% under Resolution 204/2025 unless excluded).

VAT-116.q: A business supplying non-taxable goods/services cannot deduct or reclaim the related input VAT and cannot issue VAT invoices showing a tax rate.
VAT-116.e: True. Non-taxable supplies carry no output VAT; the related input VAT is not deductible or refundable and is included in cost.
VAT-116.x:
Basis: Articles 5 and 14 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Non-taxable supplies have no output VAT; related input VAT isn't credited or refunded but expensed or capitalised. Invoices for them show no rate or VAT amount (marked 'KCT' in the e-invoice format).

VAT-117.q: An enterprise exports pre-processed green coffee (dried, hulled) bought from another trading company. The VAT rate on export is:
VAT-117.e: Exported goods qualify for 0% when contract, non-cash payment and customs declaration conditions are met; related input VAT is deductible/refundable.
VAT-117.x:
Basis: Article 9 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Pre-processed green coffee isn't a natural resource, so its export is an ordinary export at 0% with a contract, non-cash payment and customs declaration. Purchases from other enterprises (no need to declare and pay) carry no VAT, but other inputs (packaging, transport) are creditable and refundable.
Distractors: B is the domestic trading rate; C confuses it with producer sales; D is the wrong group.

VAT-118.q: Consider these VAT statements for October 2026:
VAT-118.e: F&B and professional services such as accounting/audit are reduced to 8% until 31/12/2026; telecoms is excluded; animal feed 5%.
o: Food and beverage services currently apply the 8% rate.
Accounting and audit services are taxed at 10%, reducible to 8% if not in an excluded group.
VAT-118.x:
Basis: Resolution 204/2025/QH15; Decree 174/2025/ND-CP; Article 9 of Law 48/2024/QH15.
Analysis: (1) True – food and beverage is 8% until 31/12/2026. (2) False – telecoms and IT are excluded and stay at 10%. (3) True – animal feed is 5%. (4) True – accounting and audit are 10% professional services, not excluded, so reduced to 8%.

VAT-119.q: An enterprise buys a VND 30 million batch (VAT-inclusive) from one seller, split into three VND 10 million invoices on the same day, paid in cash. The input VAT:
VAT-119.e: Each invoice is already at or above VND 5 million, so non-cash payment is required; cash payment fails the condition. The VND 20 million threshold is the old rule.
o: Is not deductible because purchases of VND 5 million or more require non-cash payment
Is deductible because each invoice is below VND 20 million
Is deductible with a cash voucher
VAT-119.x:
Basis: Article 26 of Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Each 10 million invoice is already at or above 5 million, so even without aggregation non-cash payment is required; cash means no credit. Splitting invoices with the same seller on the same day is also a threshold-avoidance red flag assessed on substance.
Distractors: B uses the old 20 million threshold; C and D have no basis (a cash voucher is not non-cash proof).

VAT-120.q: An enterprise selling only domestic goods at 10% with uncredited input VAT above VND 300 million for 12 consecutive months is entitled to a refund.
VAT-120.e: False. The 12-month/4-quarter refund applies only to producers of goods/services taxed at 5%; domestic 10% sellers carry the credit forward.
VAT-120.x:
Basis: Article 15 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: False. The 12-month/4-quarter refund applies only to producers of 5%-rated goods and services (where the input–output rate gap is structural). Domestic 10% sellers with excess credits only carry them forward.

VAT-121.q: October 2026, a credit-method enterprise sells eligible goods at a pre-tax VND 500 million and excluded-group goods (10%) at a pre-tax VND 200 million. Deductible input VAT is VND 38 million. What VAT is payable (VND million)?
VAT-121.x:
Basis: Decree 174/2025/ND-CP; Article 12 of Law 48/2024/QH15.
Working: Output = 500 × 8% + 200 × 10% = 40 + 20 = 60 million. Payable = 60 − 38 = 22 million VND.
Note: Excluded goods should be invoiced separately or line-by-line at 10% to avoid misapplying 8%.

VAT-122.q: VAT payable under the direct method on value added equals:
VAT-122.e: Used for gold, silver and gemstone trading: value added = selling payment price − corresponding purchase payment price.
VAT-122.x:
Basis: Article 13 of Law 48/2024/QH15.
Formula: VAT = value added × rate, where value added = selling payment price − corresponding buying payment price of gold, silver and gemstones.
Distractors: B is the percentage-of-revenue method; C is the credit method; D has no basis.

VAT-123.q: A gold shop on the direct value-added method has monthly jewellery sales (payment price) of VND 2,200 million and corresponding purchases of VND 1,980 million; rate 10%. What VAT is payable (VND million)?
VAT-123.e: Value added = 2,200 − 1,980 = 220 million; VAT = 220 × 10% = 22 million VND.
VAT-123.x:
Basis: Article 13 of Law 48/2024/QH15.
Working: Value added = 2,200 − 1,980 = 220 million; VAT = 220 × 10% = 22 million VND.
Note: Negative value added in a period means nothing payable and may offset positive value added later in the year per guidance.

VAT-124.q: Match each transaction with its VAT base:
VAT-124.e: Specific VAT base rules under Article 7 of the 2024 VAT Law.
p: Promotional goods compliant with commercial law
Customs value + import duty, SCT, EPT
