Transfer price minus deductible land price
VAT-124.x:
Basis: Article 7 of Law 48/2024/QH15.
Analysis: Lawful promotion – zero base (VAT-047). Instalments – one-off cash price; interest not taxable (VAT-048). Imports – customs value plus import, excise and environmental taxes (VAT-049). Property – transfer price less deductible land price (VAT-056).

VAT-125.q: The VAT base includes surcharges and additional fees retained by the business.
VAT-125.e: True. The base includes surcharges and extra fees the business is entitled to.
VAT-125.x:
Basis: Article 7 of Law 48/2024/QH15.
Analysis: True. Any surcharges and extra fees the business keeps (restaurant service charges, delivery surcharges…) are part of the price and included in the base. Exception: collections on behalf of others that aren't the business's revenue (VAT-095).

VAT-126.q: An enterprise receives VND 50 million in contract-breach compensation from a customer (not linked to a sale of goods or services). The enterprise:
VAT-126.e: Compensation not linked to sales of goods/services is not declared for VAT; the payer records a payment voucher.
o: Issues a receipt voucher; no VAT is declared or paid
VAT-126.x:
Basis: Law 48/2024/QH15; Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Contract penalty compensation isn't a sale price, so no VAT is declared; the business issues a receipt voucher and records other income (still subject to CIT).
Distractors: B and C invoice VAT on non-sales income; D has no basis.
Note: If the 'compensation' is in substance a price increase or service fee, VAT applies.

VAT-127.q: A food processor (credit method) has: (1) domestic sales of finished goods; (2) exports of finished goods; (3) sale of by-products (bran, residue) to a farm as feed; (4) supplier marketing support not linked to purchases. Select ALL transactions requiring an invoice with VAT (including 0%):
VAT-127.e: Domestic sales, exports (0%) and by-product sales require invoices; support not linked to purchases/sales is not declared for VAT.
o: (4) Support money not linked to purchases
VAT-127.x:
Basis: Law 48/2024/QH15; Decree 254/2026/ND-CP on invoices.
Analysis: (A) Domestic finished goods – VAT invoice at the applicable rate. (B) Exports – invoice at 0%. (C) By-products (bran, residues) – still sales of goods, invoiced at the product's rate (e.g., 5% if animal feed).
Distractors: (D) Marketing support not tied to purchases needs no VAT declaration – only a receipt voucher.

VAT-128.q: The 2-point VAT reduction under Resolution 204/2025/QH15 automatically continues into 2027 unless a new document is issued.
VAT-128.e: False. The resolution runs until 31/12/2026; any extension requires a new National Assembly decision.
VAT-128.x:
Basis: Resolution 204/2025/QH15.
Analysis: False. The reduction is a time-limited exception (until 31/12/2026). From 01/01/2027, absent a new resolution, the statutory 10% returns; businesses should update invoicing software.

VAT-129.q: Input VAT on a passenger car of 9 seats or fewer (not used for transport, tourism or hotel business) worth VND 2.4 billion (pre-tax) is deductible at most for the portion of value up to:
VAT-129.e: Input VAT on passenger cars of up to 9 seats (other than for transport, tourism, hotels…) is deductible only for the value up to VND 1.6 billion.
VAT-129.x:
Basis: Decree 181/2025/ND-CP (input VAT on passenger cars of up to 9 seats).
Analysis: For cars up to 9 seats not used for transport, tourism or hotel business, input VAT is creditable only on value up to 1.6 billion (excluding VAT). For a 2.4 billion car, VAT on the excess 0.8 billion isn't creditable and is capitalised.
Distractors: B ignores the cap; C has the wrong cap; D is too strict.

VAT-130.q: An enterprise buys a 7-seat car for management use at a pre-tax VND 2,000,000,000, rate 10% (not reduced). What is the maximum deductible input VAT (VND)?
VAT-130.e: Deductible only on VND 1.6 billion: 1,600,000,000 × 10% = 160,000,000 VND; the remaining 40,000,000 VND is added to cost.
VAT-130.x:
Basis: Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Working: Creditable = 1,600,000,000 × 10% = 160,000,000 VND. Invoice VAT = 200,000,000 VND; 40,000,000 VND isn't creditable and is added to the car's cost.
Note: Depreciation on cost above 1.6 billion is also non-deductible for CIT.

VAT-131.q: Which of the following services IS subject to VAT?
VAT-131.e: Advisory (including financial advisory) is taxable; credit, life insurance and securities trading are non-taxable.
VAT-131.x:
Basis: Article 5 of Law 48/2024/QH15.
Analysis: The non-taxable list names specific financial services (credit, securities business, capital transfers, life insurance…). Corporate finance advisory isn't listed, so it is taxed at 10% (8% if eligible).
Distractors: B, C and D are all in Article 5.

VAT-132.q: Arrange the steps for handling uncredited input VAT of an investment project:
VAT-132.e: Project input VAT is declared separately, offset against payable VAT; any remainder of VND 300 million or more meeting conditions may be refunded.
o: Accumulate the project's input VAT and declare it separately
Offset against VAT payable from operating activities (if any)
Compare with the VND 300 million threshold and refund conditions
File a refund claim or carry forward
VAT-132.x:
Basis: Article 15 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: (1) Declare project input VAT separately. (2) Offset against VAT payable from existing operations (offset before refund). (3) Determine the uncredited balance. (4) Compare with the 300 million threshold and refund conditions (compliant project, charter capital contributed…). (5) File a refund or carry forward.

VAT-133.q: A credit-method enterprise whose annual revenue drops below VND 1 billion must switch to the direct method.
VAT-133.e: False. Businesses (other than household/individual businesses) below VND 1 billion may voluntarily continue the credit method if bookkeeping and documentation conditions are met.
VAT-133.x:
Basis: Article 12 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: False. The 1 billion threshold makes the credit method mandatory; it doesn't force exit. Enterprises (other than household/individual businesses) below it may voluntarily stay on the credit method with full accounting and invoicing.

VAT-134.q: An enterprise leases a warehouse and collects 12 months' rent in advance (pre-tax VND 360 million) on signing. The VAT base is:
VAT-134.e: For leases with rent collected in advance for several periods, the VAT base is the total amount collected in advance.
o: Net book value of the warehouse
No VAT until the lease starts
VAT-134.x:
Basis: Article 7 of Law 48/2024/QH15.
Analysis: With 12 months prepaid, the VAT base is the full 360 million at receipt (invoicing). Accounting records unearned revenue spread at 30 million/month – a timing difference between tax and accounting.
Distractors: B is the accounting treatment, not the VAT base; C uses asset value; D is wrong as liability arises on receipt and invoicing.

VAT-135.q: When an export-processing enterprise sells goods into the domestic market, the goods bear import-stage VAT when the domestic company buys them.
VAT-135.e: True. Goods from a non-tariff zone sold into the domestic market are treated as imports; the domestic buyer clears them and pays import-stage VAT.
VAT-135.x:
Basis: Law 48/2024/QH15; Official Letter 7552/CT-QLNT of 12/10/2026.
Analysis: True. Export processing enterprises sit in non-tariff zones; their sales into the domestic market are treated as imports. The domestic buyer files an import declaration, pays import duty (if any) and import VAT, then credits it as input.

VAT-136.q: Under Official Letter 7552/CT-QLNT (12/10/2026), an export-processing enterprise enjoys non-tariff-zone treatment only when:
VAT-136.e: The EPE must be confirmed by customs as meeting customs inspection/supervision conditions; otherwise non-tariff-zone treatment does not apply.
o: Customs confirms it meets inspection and supervision conditions before it starts operating
It registers for the VAT credit method
VAT-136.x:
Basis: Official Letter 7552/CT-QLNT of 12/10/2026.
Analysis: The key condition for an export processing enterprise to enjoy non-tariff-zone treatment is customs confirmation that it meets inspection and supervision requirements before operating. Without it, it is treated as a domestic enterprise.
Distractors: B, C and D aren't legal criteria for export processing status.

VAT-137.q: A credit-method enterprise sells eligible 10% goods; the customer pays VND 108,000,000 in total. Later a 5% price reduction on the pre-tax price is granted for defects. By how much is output VAT reduced (VND)?
VAT-137.x:
Basis: Decree 174/2025/ND-CP; Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Working: Net = 108,000,000 / 1.08 = 100,000,000 VND. 5% allowance = 5,000,000 VND. Output VAT reduction = 5,000,000 × 8% = 400,000 VND, via a downward adjustment invoice; the buyer reduces input VAT accordingly.
Note: Adjustment invoices use the original invoice's rate (8%), even if issued after the reduction period.

VAT-138.q: Under the direct percentage-of-revenue method, the taxable revenue is the total payment amount (including VAT) for goods/services sold.
VAT-138.e: True. Revenue for the percentage method is the total actual sales amount on the sales invoice, including surcharges and extra fees.
VAT-138.x:
Basis: Article 13 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Under the percentage method, VAT isn't separated from price; taxable revenue is the full amount on the sales invoice (including surcharges), multiplied by the sector percentage.

VAT-139.q: Goods sold to an organisation in a non-tariff zone and consumed there (directly serving export production) are treated as exports and qualify for 0% when conditions are met.
VAT-139.e: True. Goods/services supplied to and consumed within a non-tariff zone are treated as exports and taxed at 0% with a contract, non-cash payment documents and the required records.
VAT-139.x:
Basis: Article 9 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Supplies to organisations in non-tariff zones consumed there are treated as exports at 0% with a contract, non-cash payment and required documents. Exceptions: some personal consumption services and goods not serving export production (e.g., meals, cars) don't qualify.

VAT-140.q: Consider these statements on VAT refunds in 2026:
VAT-140.e: Threshold is VND 300 million; the seller-paid condition was abolished from 01/01/2026; unrefunded amounts carry forward; import-stage VAT is not deferred.
o: The refund threshold for exports is VND 300 million.
The buyer must prove the seller paid the tax to obtain a refund.
Amounts not yet eligible for a refund are carried forward.
Import-stage VAT is eligible for deferral under Decree 245/2026/ND-CP.
VAT-140.x:
Basis: Article 15 of Law 48/2024/QH15; Law 149/2025/QH15; Decree 245/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: (1) True – 300 million threshold. (2) False – the seller-paid condition was repealed from 01/01/2026 (VAT-087). (3) True – amounts not yet refundable are carried forward. (4) False – the Decree 245/2026 deferral doesn't cover import VAT (paid per customs declaration).

VAT-141.q: For imported goods, the VAT time of determination is:
VAT-141.e: Import VAT arises on registration of the customs declaration.
o: Receipt of goods into the warehouse
VAT-141.x:
Basis: Article 8 of Law 48/2024/QH15.
Analysis: The tax point for import VAT is customs declaration registration – the same as import duty, collected by customs.
Distractors: B, C and D aren't tied to customs procedures, so they aren't the statutory tax point.

VAT-142.q: Under Official Letter 7451/CT-QLNT, allocating shared input VAT by revenue ratio applies only when the enterprise cannot account for input VAT separately by activity.
VAT-142.e: True. Where separable, input VAT is deducted on an actual basis; only the inseparable shared part is allocated by revenue ratio.
VAT-142.x:
Basis: Official Letter 7451/CT-QLNT of 07/10/2026; Decree 181/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Order of priority: (1) account inputs separately per activity; (2) only inseparable shared inputs are apportioned by revenue. Apportioning everything when separation is possible is incorrect.

VAT-143.q: Company A (credit method) sells specialised agricultural machinery to a cooperative at a pre-tax VND 600 million. The VAT on the invoice is:
VAT-143.e: From 01/7/2025, specialised agricultural machinery is taxed at 5% (not eligible for the 2-point reduction): 600 × 5% = 30 million VND.
VAT-143.x:
Basis: Article 9 of Law 48/2024/QH15.
Working: Specialised agricultural machinery is 5% from 01/07/2025 and not eligible for the 2-point cut (10% group only): 600 × 5% = 30 million VND.
Distractors: B and C apply the 10%/8% group; D is the pre-01/07/2025 regime (non-taxable).
